content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence decides to mean something.

I spill from mouths like water finding its course — sometimes a torrent, sometimes a trickle, sometimes a flood that destroys everything in its path. I am the trembling voice at the funeral. I am the shriek of the newborn. I am the lie that slides smooth as silk and the truth that catches in the throat like a bone.

Before writing ever scarred a surface, I was. I lived in firelight and died in the air, unrepeatable, each utterance a small extinction. You could never step into the same river of me twice.

I am the dictator's roar over the loudspeaker and the whispered "I love you" against skin. I am the stammer of the terrified child and the eloquence of the advocate. I build nations. I declare war. I surrender. I seduce. I betray.

I am never just words — I am rhythm, pitch, pause, volume, the catch, the crack, the crescendo. I am what the body does to language. My meaning lives as much in what I don't say, in the spaces between, in the breath held a moment too long.

You think you control me, but watch — I will escape you. I will say what you did not intend. I will reveal you. The wrong word at the wrong moment, the tone you couldn't mask, the sentence that unraveled everything.

I am humanity's oldest technology, and I am still its most dangerous.

Every time you open your mouth, you gamble on me.

*Speak.*
